newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tankan results in line with government report -- MOF.
newsitem.headline: Tankan results in line with government report -- MOF.

text.p: The result of the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) "tankan" survey of business sentiment was no different to the views expressed in the government's recent monthly economic report, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Wednesday.

"Although caution remains about future prospects, it (the tankan) showed that overall, (the economic recovery) was firm. We can see the economy is becoming more solid. The tempo is gradual, but the economy is continuing to recover," Mitsuzuka said.

The finance minister, visiting the Osaka mint, told reporters that a supplementary budget for this fiscal year to March 31 would cover necessary costs, such as reconstruction after the January 1995 Kobe earthquake and measures to cope with the food poisoning epidemic which spread throughout the nation this summer.

"Economic prospects differ according to region...It is important, from the standpoint of economic (stimulus) measures, to take into account discussions within the party and to analyse the situation," Mitsuzuka said.

He added that it would be extremely difficult to submit the supplementary budget during the extraordinary session of parliament starting on November 29, due to time constraints. Mitsuzuka said the ruling Liberal Democratic Party and the two parties in loose alliance with it were now debating Ministry of Finance (MOF) reforms. He said MOF would also try to come up with details on how to reform itself, based on an agreement among the parties.
Mitsuzuka said he had not had a chance to speak to Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto after the premier made comments about MOF reforms to reporters in Manila on Tuesday.
"I don't think the prime minister has a fixed idea yet (on MOF reforms)," Mitsuzuka said.

Hashimoto was quoted as saying on Tuesday that a new regulatory body should take over MOF's role of inspecting and supervising financial institutions and that establishing such a regulatory body within the ministry was not an option. But he also indicated that such a body should not be a powerful, fully independent body like the Fair Trade Commission.

Mitsuzuka said MOF would give advice to make sure the new bank taking over the business of the failed Hanwa Bank Ltd was established based on a policy of maintaining the credibility of the financial system and protecting depositors.
"The government and the MOF are doing all they can based on the policy of protecting depositors and I think that the credibility of Japan's financial system is being maintained," Mitsuzuka said.
